research.title: eXpath · Explaining knowledge graph link prediction
research.summary: Combines ontological closed-path rules and relational paths to explain link predictions. Two explanation-quality metrics improve by approximately 20%, with 61.4% less explanation time.
details: Develops structured explanations for embedding-based link prediction by combining relational paths with ontological closed-path rules.
Independently carried out problem formulation, method design, implementation, experiments, analysis, and writing, including rule mining and path search.
On the paper’s benchmarks, improves two explanation-quality metrics by approximately 20% and reduces explanation time by 61.4% against the best comparison methods.

research.title: RuleDep · Dependency-aware rule aggregation
research.summary: Models complementarity and redundancy among rules using sparse second-order corrections and two-stage training. Average MRR improves by about 3.7% over LR-Agg across seven datasets.
details: Models dependencies among jointly triggered rules through signed gains in log-failure evidence space, distinguishing complementary from redundant evidence.
Independently developed the method, implementation, and experiments. Implemented the core in Kotlin/JVM, using CPU multithreading and atomic operations for shared state.
RuleDep-ens raises average MRR from 0.382 to 0.396 across seven datasets, with 21 best or tied-best metrics among interpretable methods.

research.title: GeneticPrism · Hierarchical graph design and layout
research.summary: Designs multifaceted scholarly evolution graphs and the IFHL layout to jointly organize within-topic citations and cross-topic influence, evaluated through cases and a 20-participant user study.
details: Designs the GeneticPrism overview and GeneticScroll detail views for overlapping topics, temporal evolution, and cross-topic influence.
Develops Integrated Flow Hierarchical Layout (IFHL), combining internal citations and cross-topic flows through proxy nodes, weighted crossing optimization, and edge bundling.

Independently completed research design, algorithms, experiments, and writing. Three cases and a 20-participant study evaluate the approach; all seven questionnaire dimensions report p < .001 for subjective usability and perceived effectiveness.

research.title: INSPIRE · Expressive Piano Performance Generation
research.summary: Develops note-level representations, score-relative timing models, and continuous distribution prediction for expressive piano performance, covering data processing, modeling, training, and evaluation.
details: Fuses note attributes into a single Transformer timestep with typed encoding and score-relative timing deviations.
Implements custom model components and training logic with PyTorch and Transformers, spanning preprocessing, training, inference, and multi-level distributional evaluation.
On ASAP, CINR-bounded reduces PP Human-Relative Wasserstein by 15.2% against Pianist Transformer; inference cost for the reported test task decreases from 126.4 to 6.0 GPU-minutes.

research.title: CueIR · Long-term agent memory
research.summary: Studies traceable memory organization and retrieval. Memory-graph construction and agent tools are operational, with evaluation on the LoCoMo and MemoryAgentBench datasets.
